questions.stem: Rusting occurs when iron is exposed to air and water. During rusting, iron reacts with oxygen from the air to form an oxide. Some students set up this apparatus to measure the volume of oxygen in a sample of air. Each student used an excess of wet iron filings. At the start of the experiment the reading on the syringe was recorded and the apparatus was then left for a week until the reaction was completed. At the end of the experiment the reading on the syringe was recorded again.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The syringes used in one student's experiment are shown below. Record the syringe readings at the start and at the end of the experiment in the table below, and calculate the volume of oxygen used up.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The results of the other students are shown in the table.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Use the results in the table to plot a graph of volume of oxygen used up against volume of air at start. Draw a straight line of best fit.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: One of the results is anomalous. Identify this result by circling it on the graph.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Another group of students did experiments that gave several anomalous results. The teacher discussed possible errors that could have caused these anomalous results. Complete the table by choosing words from the following list to show what effect each error would have on the volume of oxygen used up. decreased increased no change

parts.label: d
